notes: Layout: four vertical L-then-C branches hang off a common top rail (columns at x~22 [L 5 / C 1], x~104 [L 6 / C 2], x~195 [L 7 / C 3], x~309 [L 8 / C 4]) and a fifth column at x~436 holds five sources in series (V-AC 9, I-AC 10, V-DC 11, I-DC 12, V-DC 13) between the top rail and the bottom rail. Four horizontal rungs run from the left-hand columns across to the taps between the sources. Net map: n1 = top rail (y~7) - the top leads of inductors 5, 6, 7, 8 and the top of V-AC 9; n2 = rung 1 (y~81) - bottom of L 5, top of C 1, bottom of V-AC 9, top of I-AC 10; n3 = rung 2 (y~166..177) - bottom of L 6, top of C 2, bottom of I-AC 10, top of V-DC 11; n4 = rung 3 (y~292..305) TOGETHER WITH the bottom rail (y~465), because rung 3 lands on the column-B wire below C 2 and that wire runs straight down to the bottom rail (junction dot at (110,465)); n4 therefore holds the bottom of C 1, the bottom of C 2, the bottom of C 4, the bottom of V-DC 11, the top of I-DC 12 and the bottom of V-DC 13; n5 = the untapped L 7 / C 3 midpoint in column C; n6 = the untapped L 8 / C 4 midpoint in column D; 0 = rung 4 (y~384..399) together with the column-C wire that runs down past the bottom rail to the GND symbol 0 - so 0 holds the bottom of C 3, the bottom of I-DC 12, the top of V-DC 13 and the GND. Judgment calls: (a) this drafter marks a real mid-wire junction with a heavy filled dot and marks a crossing with a sideways semicircular bump in the vertical. Confirmed dots: (100,166) column B on rung 2, (196,399) column C on rung 4, (110,465) column B on the bottom rail. Confirmed bumps (verified at 14-26x, clear arc with an enclosed white lune): (97,81),(180,82),(290,81) on rung 1; (178,165),(291,168) on rung 2; (187,308),(302,285) on rung 3. So each left-hand column hops every rung above its own tap - which is also the only reading that does not short the top rail to rung 1 or rung 2 and kill V-AC 9. (b) rung 3 terminates (plain T, no hop) on column B BELOW capacitor 2, not on the L7/C3 midpoint: the column-C crossing at (187,308) is an unambiguous drawn hop. Consequently rung 3 and the bottom rail are the same electrical node (n4), and the L 7 / C 3 midpoint (n5) is an untapped two-terminal node. (c) rung 4 terminates (filled dot) on column C BELOW capacitor 3, and crosses column D at (303,391) with no dot and with the column visibly jogging sideways, so I read it as a crossing: the L 8 / C 4 midpoint (n6) is likewise untapped. Every confirmed connection in this drawing carries a dot; (303,391) has none. (d) column C crosses the bottom rail at (195,464) as a PLAIN X with no junction dot and then continues down to the GND symbol. I read it as a crossing, not a junction: every other bottom-rail landing in this drawing (column A corner, column B dot at (110,465), column D terminus at (309,469)) is explicitly marked, and joining them would put both terminals of V-DC 13 on net 0 - a shorted source, i.e. a certainly wrong reading. So the bottom rail (n4) is a floating rail tied to ground only through V-DC 13 / I-DC 12, and only the column-C stub carries the ground reference. (e) V-AC 9 comes out in parallel with inductor 5 (both between n1 and n2), which simcheck reports as 'id 9 (V-AC) closes a loop of voltage sources/inductors'. This is a Tier-2 finding and it is what the ink shows: the top rail is one wire (clean T's off it at x=22, 92, 178, 291 and a corner into V-AC 9 at x=436, all verified), L 5 sits between the top rail and rung 1 (clean T at (22,83)), and the bottom lead of V-AC 9 lands on rung 1 (clean T at (437,86)). A source in parallel with an inductor is only singular for a DC operating point; this is a 3V/1kHz AC problem (all five sources are drawn as an excitation stack), so the loop is kept rather than invented away. (f) all components are two-terminal or one-terminal; terminal order is top-then-bottom as drawn and does not affect any metric. (g) no component is off-frame and none is unconnected; the inventory of 14 was used unchanged.
